alt.en: A worn, stained page of large Hebrew type with vowel points. A big word opens the top lines, and near the foot a decorated first letter, a woodcut square of leaves and scrolls, begins the last two lines.
alt.es: Página gastada y manchada, en letras hebreas grandes con signos vocálicos. Una palabra grande abre las primeras líneas y, cerca del pie, una letra inicial decorada, un cuadrado grabado en madera con hojas y volutas, empieza las dos últimas líneas.

caption.en: The opening of Adir Hu in the Haggadah printed at Prague in 1526, straight after "Chasal siddur Pesach", the words that close the seder's formal service.
caption.es: El comienzo de Adir Hu en la Hagadá impresa en Praga en 1526, justo después de "Chasal siddur Pesach", las palabras que cierran la parte formal del séder.

source: Haggadah shel Pesach (Prague Haggadah), Prague, Tevet 5287 (1526 to 1527), the page with the end of the seder and the opening of Adir Hu, cropped above the refrain

Printed in Prague in 1526/27 by Gershom and Gronem ben Solomon ha-Kohen, who died in the 16th century. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).

alt.en: A worn page of smaller type in Hebrew letters: a long line at the top, then rows of short phrases in three columns, each phrase ending in the same short word, and at the foot a long line and a short one.
alt.es: Página gastada, en letra más pequeña y con caracteres hebreos: una línea larga arriba, luego filas de frases cortas en tres columnas, cada una terminada en la misma palabra corta, y al pie una línea larga y otra corta.

caption.en: The Judeo-German Adir Hu in the same Prague Haggadah of 1526, printed in Hebrew letters below the Hebrew hymn, opening "Allmächtiger Gott" and running through its words of praise, Barmherziger, Gerechter and so on, in the order of the Hebrew alphabet.
caption.es: El Adir Hu judeoalemán en la misma Hagadá de Praga de 1526, impreso en letras hebreas debajo del himno hebreo: empieza con "Allmächtiger Gott" y recorre sus palabras de alabanza, Barmherziger, Gerechter y las demás, en el orden del alfabeto hebreo.

source: Haggadah shel Pesach (Prague Haggadah), Prague, Tevet 5287 (1526 to 1527), the page after Adir Hu, cropped to the Judeo-German version

alt.en: One line of printed music under the heading "A, ADDIR HU": a melody in 4/4 with one flat, with "Ad-dir hu yib-neh be-to be-ka-rob, bim-he-rah be-" under the notes and, in italics below, "Allmächtiger Gott, nun bau dein' Tem-pel bal-de, Ach bal-de! In".
alt.es: Una línea de música impresa bajo el título "A, ADDIR HU": una melodía en 4/4 con un bemol, con "Ad-dir hu yib-neh be-to be-ka-rob, bim-he-rah be-" bajo las notas y, debajo, en cursiva, "Allmächtiger Gott, nun bau dein' Tem-pel bal-de, Ach bal-de! In".

caption.en: The tune as J. S. Rittangel printed it at Königsberg in 1644, its earliest known printing, put into modern notation by the Jewish Encyclopedia in 1901, with the Hebrew words and the German under the notes.
caption.es: La melodía tal como la imprimió J. S. Rittangel en Königsberg en 1644, su primera impresión conocida, pasada a notación moderna por la Jewish Encyclopedia en 1901, con la letra hebrea y la alemana bajo las notas.

source: Francis L. Cohen, "Addir Hu", The Jewish Encyclopedia, vol. 1 (New York: Funk and Wagnalls, 1901), p. 187, example A, first line
library: University of California Libraries (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: IA metadata https://archive.org/metadata/jewishencycloped01sing: "possible-copyright-status": "NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT". Published in New York in 1901; the article is signed F. L. C. (Francis Lyon Cohen, died 1934); the editors died by 1940; the 1644 tune is far older (see rights.md).
credit: University of California Libraries, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: The top of a printed page of music headed "Addir Hu", "CHORUS. Maestoso" and "Traditional": a melody with three verses of transliterated Hebrew under its first line, "Addir hu, addir hu, yivneh ve-so b'-ko-rov", "Bohur hu, godol hu, yohid hu" and "Tzaddik hu, kodosh hu, rahum hu", then "bim-he-roh, bim-he-roh b'-yo-me-nu b'-ko-rov", each line over a piano part.
alt.es: La parte de arriba de una página impresa de música con el título "Addir Hu", "CHORUS. Maestoso" y "Traditional": una melodía con tres estrofas de hebreo transliterado bajo su primera línea, "Addir hu, addir hu, yivneh ve-so b'-ko-rov", "Bohur hu, godol hu, yohid hu" y "Tzaddik hu, kodosh hu, rahum hu", y luego "bim-he-roh, bim-he-roh b'-yo-me-nu b'-ko-rov", cada línea sobre una parte de piano.

caption.en: "Addir Hu" on page 81 of the revised Union Haggadah (1923), marked Maestoso and Traditional, in C major for voice and piano: the page our arrangement is read from.
caption.es: "Addir Hu" en la página 81 de la Union Haggadah revisada (1923), con las indicaciones Maestoso y Traditional, en Do mayor para voz y piano: la página de la que sale nuestro arreglo.

source: Central Conference of American Rabbis, The Union Haggadah: Home Service for the Passover, revised edition (1923), p. 81, "Addir Hu", top two systems
library: University of Florida, George A. Smathers Libraries (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Item page https://archive.org/details/unionhaggadahhom00unse: "Copyright status reviewed by UF staff - Out of copyright". Published in the US in 1923 ("COPYRIGHT 1923"), so its US term ended at the end of 2018; the setting names no arranger (the 1908 edition's Passover music was "edited by the Society of American Cantors"), so 70 years from publication in the EU and Israel (see rights.md).
